config.title: Build notification fan out service

intro.title: Build notification fan out service
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a notification fan-out service using Node.js. This service will receive a single notification request and distribute it to multiple users or channels, simulating a real-world scenario like sending alerts to a group. You'll learn how to handle asynchronous operations and manage multiple tasks concurrently. The main technologies involved are Node.js for the server environment and core JavaScript for logic and data handling. This project will help you understand how to scale simple notifications to reach many recipients efficiently.
intro.usecase: Notification fan-out services are essential in modern applications where a single event needs to trigger alerts across multiple channels. You'll see this pattern in social media platforms like Twitter or Facebook, where a new post instantly appears in followers' feeds and triggers push notifications. E-commerce sites use it to send order confirmations via email, SMS, and in-app notifications simultaneously. Customer support dashboards rely on fan-out to notify multiple agents about incoming tickets. As a developer, you'll implement these services to ensure reliable, scalable delivery of time-sensitive information across different communication methods.

objectives: Initialize a Node.js project with required dependencies for a notification service
Construct a service to send notifications via multiple channels (e.g., email, SMS)
Implement a fan-out mechanism to distribute notifications to multiple recipients
Configure a message queue to handle notification delivery asynchronously
Integrate a templating engine to customize notification content
Manipulate notification data to format it for different delivery channels
Apply error handling to manage failures in the notification pipeline

steps.title: Create helper function to add notifications
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'addNotification' that takes a 'message' parameter and adds a new notification object to the 'notifications' array. The notification object should have a unique ID (use Date.now() for simplicity) and a current timestamp (new Date().toISOString()).

steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'addNotification' that creates notification objects with unique IDs and timestamps, and adds them to the notifications array.
successCriteria: The 'addNotification' function is defined, takes a 'message' parameter, creates a notification object with 'id' and 'timestamp' properties, and pushes it to the 'notifications' array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function: 1) Takes a 'message' parameter, 2) Creates an object with 'id' (using Date.now()) and 'timestamp' (using new Date().toISOString()), and 3) Pushes it to the 'notifications' array.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes a parameter and pushes it to the subscribers array.

steps.title: Create fan-out notification function
steps.instruction: Create a function named sendNotification that takes a notification object as a parameter and sends it to all registered subscribers using HTTP requests.
steps.hint: You'll need to iterate through the subscribers array and make an HTTP request for each subscriber. You can use the fetch API or a library like axios (but for simplicity, we'll use fetch).
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named sendNotification is created that will handle sending notifications to all subscribers.
successCriteria: The sendNotification function is defined, takes a notification parameter, and contains logic to iterate through subscribers and make HTTP requests.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it takes a notification parameter and contains the logic to send to all subscribers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't match the expected structure. It should be named sendNotification and handle sending to all subscribers.

steps.expectedOutcome: A basic HTTP server is set up and ready to handle requests on port 3000.
successCriteria: The server is created with http.createServer() and listens on port 3000 with a startup log message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server setup, but make sure you're using http.createServer() and calling server.listen() with port 3000 and a callback that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server structure isn't complete. Remember to use the http module to create a server and make it listen on port 3000 with a startup message.

steps.title: Implement GET endpoint for notifications
steps.instruction: Inside your HTTP server's request handler, add a conditional block that checks if the request method is 'GET' and the URL is '/notifications'. If true, respond with your notifications array as JSON.
steps.hint: Use an if statement to check req.method and req.url, then set appropriate headers and end the response with JSON.stringify(notifications).
steps.expectedOutcome: Your server will now respond to GET requests at '/notifications' with a JSON array of all notifications.
successCriteria: The server's request handler includes an if statement that checks for GET method and '/notifications' URL, sets Content-Type header to 'application/json', and responds with JSON.stringify(notifications).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your if statement checks both the method and URL, sets the correct headers, and uses JSON.stringify on the notifications array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The GET endpoint isn't implemented correctly. Check that you're handling the request method, URL, setting headers, and returning the notifications array as JSON.

steps.hint: Check if the request method is 'POST' and the URL is '/notifications', then parse the incoming JSON data, create a notification object, add it to your notifications array, and send it to all subscribers.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your server will now accept POST requests to '/notifications' that create new notifications and send them to all subscribers.
successCriteria: POST requests to '/notifications' are handled, request body is parsed, addNotification is called with the new notification data, and sendNotification is triggered to fan-out the notification.
